title: Bounded-below descent from an acyclic weak Serre heart
statement: Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with commutative ring sheaves on sites small relative to the module-sheaf universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories and cohomology $H^j$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal A\subset\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal B\subset\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ be weak Serre subcategories, meaning strictly full subcategories containing zero and closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between their objects and under extensions. Write $D_{\mathcal A}$ and $D_{\mathcal B}$ for the full subcategories with all cohomology in these subcategories, and $D^+_{\mathcal A}$ and $D^+_{\mathcal B}$ for their bounded-below parts (cohomology zero in all degrees below some integer). Suppose $f^*$ is exact, induces an equivalence $\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, and the canonical derived unit $G\to Rf_*f^*G$ is invertible for every $G\in\mathcal B$ in degree zero. Here $Rf_*$ is total derived direct image, computed by K-injective resolutions, and $f^*=Lf^*$ is termwise exact pullback with its canonical derived adjunction. Then these functors restrict to mutually quasi-inverse equivalences $f^*:D^+_{\mathcal B}(R)\rightleftarrows D^+_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal O):Rf_*$. The canonical derived unit on $D^+_{\mathcal B}$ and counit on $D^+_{\mathcal A}$ are isomorphisms. No local cohomological bound is assumed.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^j(f^*L)\cong f^*H^j(L)$. Thus exact pullback preserves the lower bound of $L$ and carries $D^+_{\mathcal B}$ into $D^+_{\mathcal A}$, because its restriction carries $\mathcal B$ into $\mathcal A$. Hypothesis on the canonical unit applies to every $H^j(L)\in\mathcal B$; [lem-sfb-ringed-unit-from-cohomology] therefore makes $\eta_L$ invertible for every $L\in D^+_{\mathcal B}$.

For $F\in\mathcal A$, choose $G\in\mathcal B$ and $\alpha:f^*G\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ by the heart equivalence. The hypothesis $\eta_G:G[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*f^*G$ and $Rf_*\alpha$ give $Rf_*F\cong G[0]$. In particular $H^p(Rf_*F)=0$ for $p\ne0$ and $H^0(Rf_*F)\cong G\in\mathcal B$. The triangle identity gives $\varepsilon_{f^*G}\circ f^*(\eta_G)=1_{f^*G}$, whence $\varepsilon_{f^*G}=(f^*\eta_G)^{-1}$. Naturality along $\alpha$ makes $\varepsilon_F$ invertible too. This uses the actual canonical derived adjunction assumed in the statement.

The small ringed-site hypothesis lets [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] identify both module categories as Grothendieck abelian and provide the specified K-injective models. Module pullback and direct image are adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. The right adjoint preserves limits by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits], so $f_*$ is left exact: it preserves kernels and finite products, the latter being finite biproducts in these additive module categories. These are the hypotheses needed for the spectral sequence in the next step.

Let $K\in D^+_{\mathcal A}$ have cohomology zero below $a$. The standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] supplies a representative complex zero below $a$. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to $v=f_*$ and that representative. Its convergent spectral sequence has $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Rf_*H^qK)$ for $p\ge0$, zero for $p<0$, and abutment $H^{p+q}(Rf_*K)$. Step 2 makes every column except $p=0$ zero. Hence all differentials vanish. For total degree $n$ the stated finite exhaustive separated filtration has its only possible nonzero graded piece at $p=0$, namely $H^0(Rf_*H^nK)$; thus $H^n(Rf_*K)\cong H^0(Rf_*H^nK)\in\mathcal B$. For $n<a$ that piece is zero. Consequently $Rf_*K\in D^+_{\mathcal B}$. No local cohomological bound or infinite-filtration convergence is used.

For every $q$, step 2 applied to $H^q(K)\in\mathcal A$ makes its canonical derived counit invertible. Since $K$ is bounded below and $f^*$ is exact, [lem-sfb-ringed-counit-from-cohomology] applies and proves that $\varepsilon_K:f^*Rf_*K\to K$ is an isomorphism.

Both functors now preserve the specified full subcategories. Restrict their canonical derived adjunction, unit and counit to these full subcategories; the hom bijections remain the same and the triangle identities remain valid. Step 1 gives its invertible unit and step 5 its invertible counit. Their inverses and the same triangle identities exhibit mutually quasi-inverse equivalences with precisely the asserted canonical unit and counit.
